approach: Records are append-only (records.rs header, D06; gate Rule::AppendOnly), so a merge cannot edit class B's file. A merge is a NEW `athena.failure-class/1` record with status `merged` that names the class retired (`merged_from`) and the class that stays (`merged_into`). In athena-data, `ClassStatus` gains `Merged { merged_into, merged_from }` (an old `"proposed"` string still parses), `FailureClass` gains `validate()` and `merged_into_class()`, and a new `ClassMerges` type gives `resolve`, `is_retired` and `live_target`, with cycle-safe chain following. Every reader that lists or counts classes then reads through `ClassMerges`. Registry reads (introspect.rs `read_records`, labeled.rs `read_inputs`) list only live classes. Case rows and labels are mapped to the target id in memory. Recurrence grouping (hestia `class_of`), the producer brief's class summaries, evidence-label recurrence and proposal grouping resolve ids before comparing. Duplicates are stopped at creation in `apply_answer`: when the model answers `new` and the normalised name (existing `normalise`) equals the name of any live or retired class, the answer reuses the live target and writes no class record. `Athena::merge_classes(from, into)` is the library entry that checks and commits a merge record. No CLI command is added (main.rs is not a deliverable); that and the 158-class migration are marked design in the docs.

decisions.choice: A merge is a new append-only FailureClass record (status merged, with merged_into and merged_from, fresh id), not an edit of the retired class's file. Readers fold the records into a retired-to-target map.
decisions.reason: records.rs:4 says a record is written once and never modified (D06); the gate's AppendOnly rule refuses a modified records/ file (athena-gate/src/lib.rs). A new record keeps history and still meets criterion 3's 'FailureClass with status merged and merged_into'. If two merge records retire the same class, the earliest by (at, id) wins; a cycle cannot be written by merge_classes because its target must be live.

rejected.why: The gate refuses it and it breaks the records branch rule.

decisions.choice: Model the status as a data variant: `ClassStatus::Merged { merged_into: RecordId, merged_from: RecordId }` (externally tagged, so JSON reads `"status": {"merged": {...}}`), instead of two optional fields on FailureClass.
decisions.reason: A struct literal of FailureClass appears in about ten files outside the deliverables (review.rs, proposals.rs, briefs.rs tests, three cli tests); new fields would force edits in all of them. The variant also makes 'merged without a target' unrepresentable. `"proposed"` still deserializes as the unit variant. ClassStatus loses Copy; the code read uses it only as `ClassStatus::Proposed` and in assert_eq.

rejected.option: Optional merged_into and merged_from fields with skip_serializing_if
rejected.why: Edits every FailureClass literal in files outside the job and allows an inconsistent record that needs a validate rule.

rejected.why: Still touches all literals, and still needs merged_from to say which class is retired.

decisions.choice: Dedupe at creation in `apply_answer`: normalise the (boundary-reworded) new name with `introspect::normalise` and look it up in a map built by `read_records` from every non-merge class record (live or retired) to its live target. A hit reuses the target; the earlier-case check uses the reused class.
decisions.reason: Creation is where the duplicates come from, and the rule is enforced by code, not by the prompt (user default 'mechanism'). `normalise` already exists for the same purpose (cause equals what_happened).

rejected.option: Periodic clustering of the registry by a model
rejected.why: Costs tokens on every sweep, is nondeterministic, can merge unlike classes, and defaults-loop.md line 753 lists Jev pairwise merging as not decided. It can follow later using the merge record.

rejected.option: Tell the model in the prompt not to duplicate
rejected.why: Prose only; the prompt has near-zero token headroom and prompt edits are out of scope.

rejected.option: Match by description or word overlap
rejected.why: Guessing similarity with no measured threshold risks merging different causes; exact normalised name is a rule that can be tested.

rejected.option: A manual-only merge with no creation check
rejected.why: Leaves the 158-class fault unfixed at its source; every new duplicate would need a person.

decisions.choice: Resolve merges at read time, in memory. Registry reads list only live classes; case rows, labels and Jev choices map to the target. No record is rewritten.
decisions.reason: Keeps records append-only and lets the existing 158 records stand; a merge changes counts the moment its record exists.

open_questions: User: Do you want an `athena` subcommand to merge two classes now? This plan adds only the library function `Athena::merge_classes` (main.rs is not on the deliverable list), so today a merge is written by code or by hand.

User: When the 158 existing classes are merged in a later job, who picks the surviving class of each duplicate group: you from a list, or a rule such as the oldest id? The plan builds the mechanism only.

Host: Does the real registry on the records branch hold live classes whose names are equal after normalising? records/ is not in the snapshot, so the plan cannot say how many merges the normalised-name rule alone would have prevented.
